title: When the rule fails: test it with one change
outcomes: States a positional rule (rook to the open file, piece to an outpost) and the feature a position needs for it to hold
Compares a position where the rule gives a good move with one where a single change makes it fail
Says when the rule does not govern the position at all
Keeps a rule as a default with a condition, neither absolute nor discarded after one exception

steps.text: A rule of thumb is a default with conditions. "Put a rook on an open file" gives a good move in many positions and a poor one in others. To learn the condition, change one feature of a position that fits the rule and see whether the rule still gives a good move. One failure does not cancel the rule; it shows where its limit lies.

steps.caption: Black to move. The rule of thumb says: put a rook on an open file. Here it can be followed.

line.say: Rb2 follows the rule, and the engine rates it among its best moves. The rule works here.

claims.statement: The open files are: b, d.
The legal rook moves to an open file are: Rb1, Rb2, Rb3, Rb4, Rb5, Rb6, Rb7, Rbd8, Rfd8.
At depth 16 the accepted move (Rb2) is within 0.4 pawns of the best, and the best move is one of them.

steps.text: Keep each default with its condition: *take the open file, unless leaving a square costs something else*. Before you follow a rule, name what it assumes. The pair below differs by one feature, so the feature that licenses the exception can be named; the third position is one where the rule does not apply at all.

steps.title: The rule holds, the rule fails, no rule to apply
steps.prompt: Predict which statement fits each position. In the second, a Black knight has moved from d7 to f4; the third is a different position. Then name the one change that flipped the verdict between the first two.

Paper exercise (the app does not check it): pick one rule you use, such as a knight to an outpost. Write a position where it works and then one change to the position that makes it fail. That pair is your own minimal pair.
